access.edition_or_version: Penguin Classics translated by Robert Fagles

mechanics.premise: A ruler determined to purge plague from his city vows to uncover the prior king's murderer, only to discover he is the perpetrator.
mechanics.reader_promise: Rigorous dramatic irony where audience knowledge creates mounting suspense as the protagonist pursues his own doom.
mechanics.opening: The priest and supplicants appeal to Oedipus before the royal palace; established as benevolent and decisive protector.
mechanics.point_of_view: Dramatic external presentation with chorus reflecting civic and moral witness.
mechanics.character_system: Oedipus (relentless investigator), Creon (pragmatic foil), Tiresias (reluctant seer), Jocasta (desperate mediator).
mechanics.conflict_and_stakes: Public survival of Thebes versus catastrophic personal revelation and guilt.
mechanics.structure: Single-location, real-time escalation governed by progressive witness interrogation.
mechanics.scene_movement: Every scene pushes Oedipus closer to unmasking through reluctant testimonies.
mechanics.dialogue: Stichomythic interrogation where questions double as unintentional self-incriminations.
mechanics.setting: Thebes under metaphysical blight; exterior palace threshold holding civic boundary.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Dramatic irony, stichomythia, metaphorical blindness versus physical vision.
mechanics.emotional_progression: From confident civic authority to defensive paranoia, horrified comprehension, and blinding grief.
mechanics.suspense_or_anticipation: Audience watches Oedipus systematically dismantle every defense protecting him from truth.
mechanics.climax: The herdsman reveals the child given to the Corinthian messenger was Laius's son; Oedipus realizes total fulfillment of prophecy.
mechanics.ending: Self-blinding of Oedipus, exile from Thebes; chorus concludes that no mortal can be accounted happy until death.
mechanics.conventions: Aristotelian unity of action, time, and place; peripeteia coincident with anagnorisis.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Inverts conventional hero triumphant over external riddle into hero destroyed by resolving his own mystery.
mechanics.critical_reception: Praised by Aristotle as the quintessential Greek tragedy of causal necessity and tragic recognition.
mechanics.audience_reception: Universal enduring benchmark for fatalistic causal architecture and dramatic reversal.
